Well... any halfway decent network admin nowadays will tell you that using static IP ranges like that is a really bad idea for a site like 8ch. 1) it opens the servers up to attack to a much greater degree than when a load balancer/shared cloud routing is enabled simply because their IPs don't change (regardless of whether they're using IPv4 or IPv6), and 2) it's simply adequate for a site like 8chan to have a single range of IPs like that. That would ensure all of its servers are physically in one data center, meaning if something happens to that data center, it's lights out. Also, using geographically distributed servers allows end users to get the fastest response times possible - this is very important when you have a website visited by people all over the world. If you use a single IP range/datacenter, people near that datacenter might be able to get to the site easily, but those on the other side of the world will routinely find themselves connecting extremely slowly. Simply not appropriate for one of the chans.

It depends what you mean by peer to peer. ZeroNet (which had the 8ch honey pot recently) is supposedly full peer to peer and that's obviously horrible for security considering the allegations of spyware that can install cp deep into your file system. TOR ("the dark web") works through decentralized nodes but .onion sites are still susceptible to certain kinds of ddos attacks. There are a couple of other decentralized protocols for websites that might work, such as OpenBazaar2 and IPFS, but honestly I don't know enough about either one to say how well they protect against ddos attack. I will say, though, that none of the above have really caught on outside of niche communities that are, for the most part, very technical themselves. The most popular is easily TOR, but that has shown to be insecure based on the fact that law enforcement agencies control a lot of the "exit nodes" (you can google the TOR protocol if you want to understand exactly what that means). TOR is only secure if the integrity of the exit nodes can be ensured (that is one of the reasons the Silk Road guy is doing life in prison).
